verdict.unit: FALSIFIED 5/5: each named unit test PASSES on clean code, FAILS under its mutation with the same decisive line as 2026-10-04, and PASSES again on the unmodified copy; the full ./... baseline is green before and after.
verdict.live: CAUGHT 5/5: under mutation N, live negative test N FAILED each time for the guard-specific reason (g1 401->201 with an entry minted; g2 403->201 with a scopeless entry; g3 409->500; g4 replay 403->200 after a 200 disposal; g5 orphan never reaped). Restoring :dev brought the suite back to 5/5 for every guard. g1 and g2 needed a second reverted attempt, after disposing the delegation the mutation had wrongly minted. Specificity: g2-g5 failed only their own test; g1 also failed credential_use_after_revocation in the same run, as a knock-on effect of the forged child it minted.

findings: Cross-test coupling in the live suite: scope_escalation_manifest and forged_parent_signature vend with the experiments-child selectors (k8s:ns=agents, k8s:sa=nhi-exp-child). When a mutation lets one of them mint, the experiments-child pod holds two identities and credential_use_after_revocation reads whichever SVID the Workload API returns first. In all 4 observed cases the default SVID was the entry with the lexicographically smaller entry ID (g1-mutated: forged 318109b0 < revoke db07cd7e -> FAIL; g1-reverted-attempt1: 318109b0 < 4c171069 -> FAIL; g2-mutated: revoke a4eb5091 < escalate a4f8c7fb -> PASS; g2-reverted-attempt1: a4f8c7fb < d6d5270d -> FAIL). That ordering is an observed correlation, not verified in SPIRE source. The result is order-dependent knock-on failures, not a false pass of the targeted test.

The forged/escalation/replay assertions match the newest audit event by stage and outcome, not by chain_id or nonce. Under g3, the replay test matched the forged-signature test's earlier attest/deny event. It still failed correctly, on status 500 and on the reason check, but a reason-only match could in principle pick up a stale event.

Under g1, the static attest/allow audit reason ('JWT-SVID, manifest signature, nonce and child_selectors all verified') was emitted for a manifest whose signature had not verified. The audit trail asserts checks rather than recording their results.
Since the 2026-10-25 hardening, the unit suite catches g4 with 9 tests and g5 with 3 tests, not just the named one. g1, g2 and g3 are still caught by exactly one unit test each.
